plub.title: What I do at Plub
paragraphs: I'm a Data Platform Engineer at Plub. As the primary engineer, I designed and built the company's multi-tenant AWS lakehouse from scratch: S3, Glue, Athena, Lake Formation and Lambda, with dbt and Airflow for transformations.

The work ranges from reusable ingestion frameworks, so adding a new source is configuration instead of new code, to modeling with dbt, orchestrating with Airflow, and keeping everything running in production without surprises.
plub.highlightsTitle: What that looks like in practice
highlights: I moved the platform from EC2 and always-on services to serverless, with lower fixed costs and less maintenance.
Pipeline failure rate stays under 1%, with tests, alerts and retries.
Data access is immediate and self-serve, with tag-based permissions (LF-Tags): each team sees what it should without waiting on a ticket.
Transformations live in dbt, versioned and documented, instead of scattered one-off queries.

timeline.text: Multi-tenant AWS lakehouse built from scratch (S3, Glue, Athena, Lake Formation, Lambda), dbt, Airflow and data governance.
Event-driven ingestion pipelines on an AWS data lake, including Central Bank datasets. Orchestration with Airflow, plus monitoring.
AWS data lake infrastructure for digital products, and automated data quality checks.
Microservices and APIs for fintech applications, identity verification (KYC) and fraud checks.
Founded and ran a small software studio.

education.text: Natural language processing research in collaboration with Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory.
